SEEDS ON LOAN
By Hana Marzouk, our local reporter

Last Tuesday, the village of Oued Rmel opened a seed library in its old post office. Anyone can borrow a packet of vegetable seeds, grow the plants and bring back new seeds in autumn. "We started because the price of seeds had doubled," said the librarian, Mr Chaabane. The shelves held ninety packets on the first morning, and thirty families joined in the first week. "I learned more in one Saturday than in ten years," said a neighbour, Salim. Every Saturday, a retired farmer, Mrs Dhouib, explains how to plant tomatoes and peppers. The library is open from nine to noon, except on Fridays.

A pupil writes: "The seed library is open from two to five o'clock, except on Mondays." This statement is false. Which sentence corrects it with the details of the text?

options.text: It is open from nine to noon, except on Sundays.
It is open from three to six, except on Fridays.
It is open from nine to noon, except on Fridays.
It is open from three to six, except on Sundays.

questions.explanation: The last sentence of the text gives the opening hours and the closing day together. The pupil's sentence is wrong on both, so a correction must give both the right hours and the right day; an answer that fixes only one of them still contains a wrong detail.

options.text: Thirty families joined in the first month.
Thirty families joined in the first week.
Ninety families joined in the first month.
Ninety families joined in the first week.

questions.explanation: The text gives the number of families and the period together: thirty families, in the first week. options.text: Hana Marzouk
Mr Chaabane
Mrs Dhouib
Salim
a neighbour
the reporter
a retired farmer
the librarian

questions.explanation: Each name comes with a short label in the text: "our local reporter" under the title, "the librarian" before the second name, "a retired farmer" before the third and "a neighbour" before the last. What type of text is it, and what shows it?

options.text: A gardening guide: it names plants and explains how to grow them
An advertisement: it invites readers to come and borrow seeds
A news report: it tells a recent event and quotes people
A personal letter: it tells a friend what the writer did

questions.explanation: The text has a headline, a reporter's name, a recent event told in the third person and quotations from named people: these are the marks of a news report. The subject of a text does not decide its type. A guide would give instructions to the reader, an advertisement would try to persuade the reader to buy or to come, and a letter would open with a greeting to one person.

According to the text, what is the main cause of the opening of the seed library?

options.text: The village wanted a place for free lessons on planting.
Seeds had become twice as expensive as before.
The old post office needed a new use.
Many neighbours had asked the mayor for a library.

questions.explanation: The librarian gives the reason with the word "because" in his quotation: that is the cause. The other ideas are details or guesses. The lessons are one activity of the library, and the text never says that the building needed a new use or that neighbours made a request.
